subject: Urgent: Data exposure inquiry — incident notification and subprocessor coordination
messages:
From: Alice Park <alice.park@finexcorp.com>
To: dylan_brooks@redwood.com
Cc: security@finexcorp.com
Date: Fri, 20 Jun 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Possible data exposure — immediate notify window questions

Hi Dylan,

We're investigating a suspected customer-data exposure impacting a small subset of Finex test tenants. Our security team needs to understand Redwood's incident notification obligations under the active DPA and whether any subprocessors were involved in the affected flow.

Specifically we need:
- Confirmation of the notification window Redwood adheres to for potential unauthorized access (contract language reference is fine)
- Scope definition: does Redwood consider this an "incident" triggering DPA notification when limited to non-production test tenants?
- List of subprocessors active in the environment that processed Finex data in the last 30 days (or an access path to a current subprocessor roster)
- ETA for transfer of forensic logs and minimal evidence to support our investigation (S3 bundle or secure share)

Can you put together a short plan and timeline? Finex legal and InfoSec are standing by; we may need an executed DPA amendment depending on findings.

Thanks,
Alice
Alice Park
Head of Security Ops | Finex Corp

From: dylan_brooks@redwood.com
To: Alice Park <alice.park@finexcorp.com>
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 20 Jun 2025 09:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Possible data exposure — immediate notify window questions

Alice — thanks for the quick heads-up. We're treating this with high priority. Internal ops notes below and proposed next steps.

Quick answers (high level):
- Notification window: Redwood's standard DPA incident notification is "as soon as reasonably practicable" but we commit to an initial contact within 72 hours for confirmed unauthorized access. For suspected exposures we provide an initial status within 24 hours of being notified and an updated timeline within 72 hours. I will attach the DPA reference clause in the follow-up.
- Scope: Non-production/test tenants are covered under the DPA where Finex data is involved; however the materiality and customer impact will determine whether it triggers the formal notification flow. We'll treat this as a potential incident until we can rule it out.
- Subprocessors: We maintain a live roster; I can provide the list for the last 30 days and mark which components processed Finex traffic.
- Evidence transfer: we can generate a minimal forensic bundle (logs + KV-cache dump pointers + request IDs) and provide via a secure Drive link or SFTP. Expect initial bundle in ~48 hours, with prioritized extracts in 12–24 hours if you need quicker context.

Proposed short M.A.P. (mutual action plan):
1) Redwood to confirm scope and initial evidence packet: 12–48 hours
2) Finex to specify priority time ranges and any identifying request IDs or user IDs: 12 hours
3) Joint call to align on further evidence needs and DPA/contract implications: within 24–36 hours
4) If formal notification is required, Redwood legal to draft notice and proposed DPA amendment/escrow steps: within 72 hours

Monica / Karthik / Lauren — looping you in for evidence generation, subprocessor list, and legal redline readiness.

I'll follow up with the DPA clause and an S3 share link once we start preparing logs.

—Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Customer Reliability Manager | Redwood Inference

From: monica_patel@redwood.com
To: Alice Park <alice.park@finexcorp.com>, dylan_brooks@redwood.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 20 Jun 2025 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Possible data exposure — initial evidence plan and subprocessors

Hi Alice / Dylan,

We've started the evidence collection. Summary of what we'll share in the first wave (attachment stubbed):
- Forensic_log_summary.zip (redacted where appropriate) — contains request IDs, timestamps, and affected tenant tags
- proposed_map_subprocessors.csv — CSV mapping service/component -> subprocessor -> processing role -> last-30d activity flag
- short readme.txt with access instructions and retention limitations

Notes on subprocessors:
- Storage: Redwood uses CloudStore Inc. (US) for transient artifact storage; access is restricted and audited.
- Observability: metrics/log aggregation handled by LogStream Ltd. (logs contain request metadata but no decrypted PII fields)
- Model infra: dedicated model hosts are run in Redwood-managed pools; we do not use third-party model providers for this hosted environment.

A few operational clarifications:
- Evidence export is time-boxed: we'll provide an initial S3 share for 14 days. If Finex requires longer custody for legal review, we should document the retention extension in the M.A.P.
- Cross-border transfer: if any forensic artifacts include EU-resident data or identifiers that trigger transfer controls, we'll need to coordinate with legal. Please flag any account-specific regionality.

Requesting Finex to confirm priority windows and whether you want an NDA/DPA amendment in advance of receiving the bundle. Once we have that, we can add a narrow access control (SAML link) to the share.

Attachments: forensic_log_summary.zip (attachment stub), proposed_map_subprocessors.csv (attachment stub)

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Director, Trust & Security | Redwood Inference

From: dylan_brooks@redwood.com
To: Alice Park <alice.park@finexcorp.com>, monica_patel@redwood.com
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 21 Jun 2025 10:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Possible data exposure — incident notification and subprocessor coordination

Alice — confirming next steps following Monica's initial packet.

Summary / agreed actions:
- Redwood to deliver prioritized log extracts (identifiers + request traces) by 2025-06-21 18:00 UTC. Full forensic bundle to follow within 48 hours (shared Drive link).
- Monica to include the subprocessor CSV and highlight components that touched Finex tenant IDs. See attached stub.
- Legal: Lauren will prepare a narrow DPA amendment template and a short addendum that clarifies notification timing for suspected non-prod exposures; draft available by 2025-06-22 EOD.
- Access control: temporary SAML-protected share; Finex to confirm list of security contacts who need access.

If Finex confirms they want formal written notice at this stage (even if unconfirmed), we'll move forward with the notification draft and evidence hand-off under an expedited review. Otherwise we'll proceed with the investigative bundle and reconvene after initial findings.

Proposed call: 2025-06-21 16:00 UTC (30 min) — please confirm or propose an alternative.

Regards,
Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Customer Reliability Manager | Redwood Inference
